hook_2s: 9/10: 'Model updated. Memo and deck still wrong.' immediately names the cross-file mismatch I dread; the green Excel number beside two red failures makes it concrete.

issues.evidence: The panel says '10 of 10 changes accepted', and the final memo shows €74.6m in its paragraph and table. But the slide 2 box David flagged is never shown corrected. His satisfied board-meeting reaction supplies emotional closure without proving that specific fix.
issues.suggested_action: Once the pending real recording exists, show the corrected slide 2 TextBox 23 at €74.6m and the updated dependent chart before Maya closes the laptop; replace some review-panel coverage to make room.

issues.evidence: The hook already marks the model updated at €74.6m, then 'Step 1 of 3, by hand' shows entering 8.5. Later the request says 'Take DACH Q4 down to 8.5', while the memo outlook rises from €71–73m to €74.6m. As a finance user, I pause to reconcile the sequence and direction.
issues.suggested_action: Frame the opening explicitly as the failed-workflow result, and add a short clarification that €71–73m is stale published guidance while €74.6m is the recalculated scenario; preserve the approved demo numbers.

issues.evidence: Maya at 00:12 has visibly different facial proportions and hair framing from the close-up at 00:29 and the review shot at 00:50. The later shots read more consistently with one another. This weakens my sense that I am following one colleague through the same night.
issues.suggested_action: Verify continuity in motion first; if the difference remains noticeable, replace the 00:12 shot with a matching take or use a hands-and-laptop crop.

issues.evidence: The flagged TextBox 23 change is readable, but subsequent rows include truncated descriptions such as 'Midpoint shown → R...' and 'mid-market growth ...'. The highlighted accept/reject controls demonstrate control, but I cannot assess the wording I would be approving.
issues.suggested_action: Open one dependent chart or text diff in the real app and hold its complete before-and-after content long enough to read, replacing one panel scroll.

issues.evidence: The close-up after 'Partner flagged this' reads as subdued disappointment rather than overt melodrama, which helps. However, the reaction is softer and more portrait-like than the earlier working shot; the message itself already carries the professional sting.
issues.suggested_action: Verify the silent reaction in motion; retain a brief glance and contained reset, and shorten any lingering hurt expression so the return to review feels practical.

top_revision: Show the actual corrected slide 2 box and dependent chart after acceptance, so the film proves the precise failure that made me care.
purchase_objections: I see proposed changes and acceptance, but not the corrected deck object that caused the escalation.
I need to test whether it preserves my existing templates and handles dependencies across my own pack.
The multi-file Changes panel distinguishes this from my current AI tools, but I need evidence that reviewing it replaces enough manual reconciliation to justify another subscription.
would_try: yes — The stale table, wrong-template deck and partner escalation feel familiar, and grouped changes across my real files are worth testing.
buy_decision: NOT_BUY — I am not yet convinced the whole pack is reconciled; the single thing that would flip me to BUY is a successful trial on my own pack showing the model, memo, flagged deck box and dependent chart all agree after acceptance.
